profiles.name: HamSammich
profiles.profile: This is the kind of file where the wedges keep showing up to bail out a round that the rest of the bag is actively trying to murder. The profile is a little split-brain: one appearance had the putter face plant hard, the next looked way more survivable because the short game did the heavy lifting and the flatstick stopped bleeding quite as much. The irons are the suspicious part here; when the approaches are off, everything gets ugly fast. If the rest of the bag ever stops being a liability, there’s a player hiding in here.

profiles.name: tnboles77
profiles.profile: This one’s a weird little survival act: the tee ball keeps trying to sabotage the whole afternoon, and somehow the hands around the greens keep dragging the corpse back to life. The short game and putter have been loud enough to mask a lot of ugliness, which is why the card can look cleaner than the swing deserves. When the driver and irons show up looking responsible, the score can get spicy fast. When they don’t, it turns into damage control with extra plot twists.

profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.tagline: TEE BALL WEAPON, IRONS ON LEASH
profiles.profile: This file is basically a truck with a nitrous kit: when the driver gets cooking, the whole operation turns into a stress test for the field. The underlying ball-striking has been absurdly strong across the window, and the putter is good enough that this thing doesn’t need miracles. Even the ugly stuff is usually relative, which is a nice problem to have in a league full of guys making pars look like hostage negotiations. If there’s a flaw, it’s that the bar is so high that anything less than nuclear looks almost rude.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.tagline: APPROACH GAME WITH A VISE GRIP
profiles.profile: This is the cleanest all-around file in the batch, and it’s not subtle about it. The irons keep dictating terms, the tee ball is plenty rude, and the scoring chances come in bunches instead of from wishful thinking and prayer. There’s enough short-game pop here to patch the occasional mess, which is why the card keeps staying out of the ditch. In other words: not flashy chaos, just a very annoying player who keeps showing up with the right answer.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.profile: The interesting part here is that the scoring is showing up even when the ball-striking isn’t exactly setting the building on fire. The putter has been the loudest club in the bag, with enough help from the front end to keep the round from turning into a full clown show. There’s power here, too, which is why the profile has a little ceiling baked into it instead of pure grindball nonsense. Still, the identity is pretty clear: if the putter’s hot, the rest of the bag gets to pretend it’s part of the plan.

profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.profile: This is the sort of file that makes a grown man stare at the bars and mutter, “how is this still in the fairway of life?” The shapes are ugly in a few different directions at once: tee game leaking, short game leaking, and the putter not exactly showing up with a cape. There are a couple moments where the approach play flickers just enough to remind you the bag isn’t totally dead, but the overall vibe is survival mode with extra doubles. It’s volatile in the worst possible way — enough evidence to hurt your feelings, not enough to promise a clean fix.
